title: More from Less: 3D Gaussian Splatting Digital Twins with Iterative Expansion and Trajectory Compensation for Sparse-Demonstration Bimanual Manipulation
abstract_en: Sparse bimanual demonstrations cover limited object states and contact configurations. More from Less combines structured action prediction, failure-region expansion, and local recovery. A vision–language–action (VLA) policy predicts joint action chunks with shared context and training-only geometric supervision. Object-level 3D Gaussian Splatting supplies appearance assets for physical proxies with separate collision geometry and assigned physics. Policy failures locate regions for virtual rollouts. Only complete trajectories passing task, physics, and safety checks enter real-dominated retraining. During deployment, asynchronous video references provide image-plane targets for current-state mapping and gated fusion. Base and fused actions pass through a shared quadratic program and nonlinear recheck. Across six real-robot task categories, Full Pipeline reaches a four-stage macro-average success rate of 89.00%, compared with 75.83% for Structured Dual-arm VLA. This comparison measures stage-level outcomes of the combined system, rather than complete-task success.
manuscript_status: Research manuscript; no journal acceptance is claimed

figures.caption_latex: The More from Less closed-loop framework. Structured bimanual VLA learns joint action chunks from sparse real demonstrations. Object-level 3DGS proxies support failure-guided expansion; only successful complete trajectories passing task, physics, and safety acceptance enter real-dominant retraining. At deployment, valid low-frequency references can compensate high-risk steps. Both base and fused actions pass through the shared QP and nonlinear recheck. The schematic layout was initially explored with imagegen and subsequently rebuilt in PowerPoint.
figures.source_note: Retained manuscript figure; published path and checksum identify the release asset. Workstation-only source paths are omitted.

figures.caption_latex: Structured bimanual VLA. Synchronized global and wrist RGB images, language, and joint states produce a joint 32-step chunk of 12-dimensional absolute targets. Predicted and demonstrated actions use the same relation mapping and normalization. The two action-dependent relation maps contain pose and distance. Contact and role labels appear separately in the shared training context; they remain fixed and produce no action gradient. The schematic layout was initially explored with imagegen and subsequently rebuilt in PowerPoint.

figures.caption_latex: Object-level proxies and failure-guided expansion. Top: calibrated RGB and masks yield 3DGS visual assets, combined with simplified collision assets and recorded physics in Isaac Sim. Bottom: failures locate feasible sampling neighborhoods. Only successful complete trajectories passing joint acceptance enter real-dominant retraining. Optional residual RL proposes simulation candidates subject to the same acceptance; it is not deployed on the robot. The schematic layout was initially explored with imagegen and subsequently rebuilt in PowerPoint.

figures.caption_latex: Step-level compensation and shared safety filtering. High risk requests an asynchronous 2D reference. Current-state alignment, depth and calibration, task-masked DLS IK, and validity checks precede gated fusion. Low risk, waiting, or invalidity sets the fusion weight to zero. All actions pass through the shared QP and nonlinear recheck; failure causes slowdown or hold. Grippers inherit VLA targets; unobserved orientation has no exact-preservation guarantee. The schematic layout was initially explored with imagegen and subsequently rebuilt in PowerPoint.

figures.caption_latex: Numerical diagnostics of offline pouring and board-wiping trajectories. Each row represents one clip, and n denotes the trajectory-point count. The three columns show the camera-frame XY path, modeled depth Z, and 3-D Euclidean distance to the retargeted trajectory R. G denotes the trajectory extracted from the generated video and mapped into 3-D; F denotes the offline fused trajectory. The XY axes have equal scales, and curves are not independently normalized. Time is the relative sampling time of the target generated clip.
